summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and a chronic left hip pressure ulcer, was admitted for generalized weakness and fever initially suspected to be a urinary tract infection. However, urine culture was negative, and elevated inflammatory markers along with imaging findings raised concern for osteomyelitis. A bone biopsy was performed, and wound culture grew MRSA, leading to a diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis of the left ischium. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral doxycycline. Due to ongoing wound care needs, malnutrition, and limited home support, he was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation, wound management, and antibiotic completion. His multiple sclerosis and depression were managed supportively during admission.
